answer: Persistent workload ledger. Each identity must sustain a rolling history of completed tasks whose resource signature (compute-time, storage churn) is logged against a slowly decaying baseline, like sediment settling in karst. A clone starts with zero history, so it must grind real work to match the baseline before earning task priority—making fakery cost more than honest participation. The ledger also cross-checks against a comet-like burst detector, flagging new identities that spike faster than shale-thin growth curves allow. Attacker cost: full baseline work per clone.
